subject: Dedicated Capacity pricing follow-up / sizing (AcuityHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + sizing questions (Dedicated capacity)

Thanks again for the call today, Sarah — great to meet you and hear more about how AcuityHealth is planning to roll LLM-powered triage and summarization into your clinician workflows. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the open items and clarify a few sizing/pricing assumptions so we can get a scoped quote over to procurement next week.

Key points / notes from call:
- Target workload: real-time triage + note summarization for ~900 clinicians, peak 10k requests/day, expected average request size ~1.2k tokens in / out (prompt + response).
- Monthly token volume (current estimate): 300M - 900M tokens/month as you ramp over 6 months.
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile < 400ms per request for short tasks; batchable longer jobs okay for nightly summarization.
- Preferred GPU: you mentioned a preference for A100 80GB for stability, but open to H100 if unit economics are favorable.

Sizing questions for Marcus / engineering follow-up (to confirm):
1) Given the 1.2k token avg and desirable P95 <400ms, what is the expected throughput per GPU for using a gpt-style open model (quantized)?
2) If we reserve 4x A100-80GB, does that meet peak of ~10k requests/day with headroom for burst?
3) What are the tradeoffs for using H100 (faster single-request latency) vs A100 (cost/availability)?

Pricing / budget signals from Sarah: you indicated a monthly budget band of ~$25k–$60k initially, and a target unit economics of roughly $2.5k–$3.5k per 1M tokens once in steady-state. Confirming that so we can tune the proposal.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marcus to share a quick capacity calc and recommended reserved size + GPU type (by Thu PST).
- I’ll assemble a draft pricing PDF with two options (2x/4x/8x A100 and equivalent H100 options) for procurement.
- Sarah to loop in procurement contact (if any) and share timing for legal review.

Attachments: none in this email — will follow with capacity calc and pricing PDF.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing questions (Dedicated capacity)

Marissa / Sarah — quick follow-up with the capacity sketch (attached). Highlights:

- Throughput estimates (approx, using a quantized 7B/13B open model on A100-80GB):
  - Single A100-80GB (dedicated, optimized runtime): ~1200–1500 tokens/sec steady-state with continuous batching for small requests; for single-request latency we see ~150–220 ms per 1.2k token response depending on model variant.
  - H100 tends to reduce latency ~20–30% for large-context workloads (and gives better perf for FP16 kernels), but has higher hourly cost in most clouds today.

- Recommended reserved pools (starting point):
  - Conservative: 2x A100-80GB — handles ~2.4M tokens/hr (~57.6M tokens/day) with moderate queuing at peaks; good if you plan to route low-priority work to burst.
  - Balanced: 4x A100-80GB — supports ~4.8M tokens/hr (~115M/day) with headroom for your 10k req/day profile and nightly summarization.
  - Aggressive: 8x A100-80GB — for >200M tokens/day sustained workloads.

- Cost levers: model size, batching windows, and use of KV/prefix cache (common prompts) will materially reduce per-token cost. If you can cache clinician templates / prompt prefixes, effective tokens billed per useful output drops.

Attaching: capacity_calc_acuity.xlsx (token throughput by GPU, sample traffic curves). I’ll join the technical deep-dive if you want to get into model variants and kernel choices.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing questions (Dedicated capacity)

Thanks Marissa / Marcus — this is helpful. Sharing a few clarifications from our side:

- The 10k requests/day is a near-term estimate; over 6 months we expect the active clinician count to grow and could hit 25k requests/day in Q3.
- We are comfortable starting with the balanced option (4x A100-80GB) if pricing works — gives us room to ramp without immediate rearchitecture.
- Procurement loop: adding Mike Chen (cc’d) as procurement lead. Mike, our initial asks are: SLA overview, standard MSA + SOW, and a ballpark quote we can use for internal approvals.

Budget confirmation: leadership wants to see a steady-state target of $2,500–$3,500 per 1M tokens. For initial pilot we have ~ $30k/month to cover Feb–Apr.

Happy to schedule a 30-min procurement/ops sync next week if that helps.

—Sarah
Sarah Johnson
Director of Digital Health, AcuityHealth

Hi Sarah / Mike — looping in a pricing sketch PDF (redwood_dedicated_pricing_ACUITY_v1.pdf) with three configurations: 2x / 4x / 8x A100-80GB and an appendix showing H100-equivalent options. Notes:

- 4x A100-80GB (reserved monthly) — estimated list price: $38k/mo. This assumes a mid-sized open model with quantization optimizations and the caching configurations Marcus suggested. Effective unit cost: ~$3,200 per 1M tokens at ~115M tokens/day sustained numbers — this aligns with your steady-state target range.
- H100 equivalent (4x) typically increases instance cost ~15–25% but reduces latency; we can provide both line items.
- Discounts: we can reduce list by ~10–20% depending on 12mo commit and model licensing.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_ACUITY_v1.pdf (pricing options). I’ve also included the capacity calc Marcus attached in the previous email.

Next steps:
- Marissa: confirm that the 4x A100 sketch is acceptable for pilot so I can produce a formal quote and SOW.
- Mike / procurement: let us know required contracting cadence (MSA + SOW, or PO + SOW) and any specific compliance / SOC2 evidence you need.

Thanks — Vanessa
